text: There was once a Prince who wished to marry a Princess; but then she must be a real Princess. He travelled all over the world in hopes of finding such a lady; but there was always something wrong. Princesses he found in plenty; but whether they were real Princesses it was impossible for him to decide, for now one thing, now another, seemed to him not quite right about the ladies. At last he returned to his palace quite cast down, because he wished so much to have a real Princess for his wife. One evening a fearful tempest arose, it thundered and lightened, and the rain poured down from the sky in torrents: besides, it was as dark as pitch. All at once there was heard a violent knocking at the door, and the old King, the Prince's father, went out himself to open it. It was a Princess who was standing outside the door. What with the rain and the wind, she was in a sad condition; the water trickled down from her hair, and her clothes clung to her body. She said she was a real Princess. “Ah! we shall soon see that!” thought the old Queen-mother; however, she said not a word of what she was going to do; but went quietly into the bedroom, took all the bed-clothes off the bed, and put three little peas on the bedstead. She then laid twenty mattresses one upon another over the three peas, and put twenty feather beds over the mattresses. Upon this bed the Princess was to pass the night. The next morning she was asked how she had slept. “Oh, very badly indeed!” she replied. “I have scarcely closed my eyes the whole night through. I do not know what was in my bed, but I had something hard under me, and am all over black and blue. It has hurt me so much!” Now it was plain that the lady must be a real Princess, since she had been able to feel the three little peas through the twenty mattresses and twenty feather beds. None but a real Princess could have had such a delicate sense of feeling. The Prince accordingly made her his wife; being now convinced that he had found a real Princess. The three peas were however put into the cabinet of curiosities, where they are still to be seen, provided they are not lost. Wasn't this a lady of real delicacy?

sentences.physical_context: The Prince is traveling in search of a real Princess.
sentences.korean: 옛날에 한 왕자가 있었는데, 그는 공주와 결혼하고 싶어했습니다. 하지만 그녀는 진짜 공주여야 했습니다.

sentences.physical_context: The Prince travels extensively but finds something wrong with each princess.
sentences.korean: 그는 그런 여인을 찾기 위해 전 세계를 여행했습니다. 하지만 항상 뭔가 잘못된 점이 있었습니다.

sentences.physical_context: The Prince finds many princesses but doubts their authenticity.
sentences.korean: 공주들은 많았지만, 그들이 진짜 공주인지 판단하기가 불가능했습니다. 왜냐하면 이러저러한 점이 그에게는 항상 뭔가 맞지 않게 느껴졌기 때문입니다.

sentences.physical_context: The Prince returns home feeling downcast.
sentences.korean: 마침내 그는 진짜 공주를 아내로 삼고 싶었기 때문에 완전히 낙담한 채 궁전으로 돌아왔습니다.

sentences.physical_context: A fierce storm with thunder, lightning, and heavy rain begins.
sentences.korean: 어느 날 저녁, 무서운 폭풍이 일어났고, 천둥과 번개가 치고, 비가 하늘에서 쏟아졌습니다. 게다가 칠흑같이 어두웠습니다.

sentences.physical_context: There is a violent knocking at the door during the storm.
sentences.korean: 갑자기 문을 두드리는 격렬한 소리가 들렸고, 왕자의 아버지인 늙은 왕이 직접 나가서 문을 열었습니다.

sentences.physical_context: A Princess is found standing outside in the storm.
sentences.korean: 문 밖에는 한 공주가 서 있었습니다.

sentences.physical_context: The Princess is drenched and in poor condition from the storm.
sentences.korean: 비와 바람 때문에 그녀는 비참한 상태였습니다. 물이 그녀의 머리에서 흘러내렸고, 옷은 몸에 달라붙었습니다.

sentences.physical_context: The Princess claims to be a real Princess.
sentences.korean: 그녀는 자신이 진짜 공주라고 말했습니다.

sentences.physical_context: The Queen-mother secretly prepares a test with peas under the bed.
sentences.korean: “아! 곧 알게 될 거야!”라고 늙은 왕비는 생각했습니다. 그러나 그녀는 무엇을 할 것인지에 대해 한마디도 하지 않고 조용히 침실로 가서 침대에서 모든 침구를 걷어내고 침대에 작은 콩 세 개를 놓았습니다.

sentences.physical_context: The Queen-mother stacks mattresses and feather beds over the peas.
sentences.korean: 그런 다음 그녀는 그 세 개의 콩 위에 매트리스를 스무 개 쌓고, 그 위에 깃털 침대를 스무 개 더 올렸습니다.

sentences.physical_context: The Princess is to sleep on the prepared bed.
sentences.korean: 이 침대에서 공주는 밤을 보내야 했습니다.

sentences.physical_context: The Princess is asked about her sleep quality.
sentences.korean: 다음 날 아침 그녀에게 어떻게 잤는지 물었습니다.

sentences.physical_context: The Princess complains about her poor sleep.
sentences.korean: “아주 나쁘게 잤어요!” 그녀가 대답했습니다.

sentences.physical_context: The Princess explains she barely slept.
sentences.korean: “밤새 거의 눈을 감지 못했어요.

sentences.physical_context: The Princess describes feeling something hard under her.
sentences.korean: 침대에 무엇이 있었는지 모르겠지만, 아래에 딱딱한 것이 있었고, 온몸이 멍들었어요.

sentences.physical_context: The Princess expresses how much the discomfort hurt her.
sentences.korean: 너무 아팠어요!

sentences.physical_context: It is revealed that the Princess felt the peas through the bedding.
sentences.korean: 이제 그녀가 스무 개의 매트리스와 스무 개의 깃털 침대 너머로 작은 콩 세 개를 느낄 수 있었기 때문에 그 여인이 진짜 공주임이 분명해졌습니다.

sentences.physical_context: The Princess's sensitivity is praised as proof of her royalty.
sentences.korean: 진짜 공주만이 그렇게 섬세한 감각을 가질 수 있었습니다.

sentences.physical_context: The Prince decides to marry the Princess.
sentences.korean: 왕자는 그녀가 진짜 공주임을 확신하고 그녀를 아내로 삼았습니다.

sentences.physical_context: The peas are kept as a curiosity.
sentences.korean: 그러나 그 세 개의 콩은 호기심의 캐비닛에 보관되어 있으며, 잃어버리지 않았다면 아직도 볼 수 있습니다.

sentences.physical_context: The story concludes by reflecting on the Princess's delicacy.
sentences.korean: 이 여인이 진짜 섬세한 여인이 아니었나요?
